parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the ESM .mjs, /output, local-import-only, manual --a parsing, no binary-buffer interfaces, bencode decode, and Python repr parity requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It first probed behavior, then assigned four separate child owners for decoder, pyrepr, argparse, and entry files while retaining final integration and verification in the parent.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote the initial file set under a shared tagged-value contract; after integrated comparison failures, the parent edited /output/lib/decoder.mjs to add the invalid-leading-byte stdout side effect and dict key-drop behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent consumed the AgentSwarm result, ran the assembled /output/test4.mjs against the reference executable, patched the decoder, reran comparison to ALL MATCH, and delivered four files.
parallel.verification: Parallel verification included pre-delegation black-box probes, child syntax checks, child local tests, and a final broad stdout/exit-code comparison after the parent fix.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed the delivered artifact at 47/57; the allowed pair data does not include the hidden failing case identities, and no post-final visible mismatch remained in the trajectory.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same ESM .mjs, /output, manual parsing, no-dependency, black-box, bencode behavior, ASCII encoding, and Python repr requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, integration, correction, verification, and final delivery without any child delegation or handoff boundary.
serial.implementation: It wrote a six-file module tree with argparse, ASCII codec, Python-style errors, decoder, repr formatter, and entry file, then edited decoder and argparse after comparison mismatches.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All modules were produced and reconciled locally by the same actor, with the final file list including test4.mjs and five library files.
serial.verification: Serial verification included sample probes, edge-case probes, a 57-case comparison harness, extra argparse probes, and final sample confirmation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator also failed the serial artifact at 47/57; the available pair files do not reveal which 10 official cases failed.

comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement coverage difference is visible for the official outcome; serial captured ASCII/error modules explicitly while parallel encoded those behaviors more narrowly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split ownership across four children, one each for decoder, pyrepr, argparse, and entry, with parent integration afterward.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation, correction, and delivery ownership in the main actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel decomposition created a child-brief boundary for decoder behavior; serial had no comparable handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel provided a shared tagged-value contract and per-file child specs, but the decoder brief reduced the invalid-leading-byte behavior to an AssertionError only.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained probe observations and implementation details in one actor, so corrections did not cross a child brief or handoff boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main context difference is the decoder child's incomplete behavioral brief; the cross-file tagged-value interface itself was explicit and did not break.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children produced the initial module set, then the parent patched /output/lib/decoder.mjs after integrated comparison mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the full module tree itself and patched /output/lib/bencode/decoder.mjs plus /output/lib/argparse.mjs after local mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had parent takeover of a child-written decoder file; serial performed equivalent corrections inside the original single implementation context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All four child agents completed and returned summaries in the AgentSwarm aggregate before parent integration.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results; the main actor carried all work through to final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a real child result lifecycle but no missing join or trapped result; serial had no delegation lifecycle to manage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote separate assigned files in the same /output tree and the parent assembled them through imports and end-to-end execution.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all final files directly and confirmed the final file list from one owner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared the workspace but used non-overlapping file scopes; no same-file collision or overwrite was observed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran child syntax checks, then parent integrated testing that first exposed diffs and finally reported ALL MATCH after the decoder patch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran a 57-case harness, saw six mismatches, edited, reran to pass=57 fail=0, and confirmed the sample cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on self-generated black-box tests rather than the hidden official suite; parallel's verification crossed the child integration boundary, while serial's stayed local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished without process timeout after 1139.12 agent seconds and had 145 seconds remaining in the retry budget.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished without process timeout after 671.379 agent seconds and had 1726 seconds remaining in its budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more time and budget due to delegation and post-join correction, but still closed normally; the official pass/fail relation remained the same.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome in the current completed status records: both parallel and serial have solution_passed false and task_result 47/57. The concrete task-solving difference is that parallel delegated four modules and needed parent rework of the child decoder after an integration mismatch, while serial implemented and fixed all modules in one actor. Because both official evaluations failed at the same score and the allowed pair files expose only aggregate official results, the shared official failure cannot be attributed to the retained coordination episode.
parallel_contributors: Parallel used four child file owners under a shared tagged-value contract and then parent integration testing corrected the child decoder.
Parallel delivered a four-file tree and reported an ALL MATCH self-comparison before closure.
serial_contributors: Serial retained implementation and correction in one context and delivered a six-file tree with ASCII and Python-error helper modules.
Serial also reported pass=57 fail=0 on its self-generated comparison harness before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel assumed ASCII string input in the shared contract, while serial wrote an explicit ASCII codec helper.
Parallel kept simple Error messages, while serial added Python-style error helper types; the official failure details are not available in the allowed pair files.
evaluator_effects: The official summaries expose only aggregate 47/57 results, not the identities of the ten failing cases.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel adverse process consequence only; no evidenced outcome differential
